question.problem: Find a basis of $\,\text{Ker}(T)$ given that $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2x-y \\ 5x-3y \\ x+3y\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
Finding the kernel of $\,T\,$ is equivalent to finding the null space of the standard matrix of $\,T.$

For the given linear transformation, the standard matrix is $T=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 0 \\ 5 & -3 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}].$

Setting $x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}],$ we then need to solve the equation $Tx=0.$ First, we reduce $T$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 0 \\ 5 & -3 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & ↔{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 5 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -18 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -18 & 0 \\ 0 & -7 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-\frac{7}{18}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -18 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$ and $y$, and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$

From the second equation, we get $y=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we have $x=0.$ 

Therefore, if $x\in \text{Ker}(T),$ then 

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]z,\,z\in R.
$$

This implies that $B={[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}$ is a basis of $\text{Ker}(T).$
